corePhenomenon: What can you honestly say about this hollow from what you actually saw, measured, and tested?

puzzles.name: Where Did Last Night's Water Go?

westface-slope.prompt: Rills score the slope. Which way did last night's water actually go?

options.label: It stayed on this slope
options.hint: The rills run toward lower ground. Walk that way.

options.label: Toward the top of Granite Knob
options.hint: Water does not climb the knob. Look at the rills.

high-look.prompt: From here the hollow tilts. Where should last night's water still linger?

options.label: The pond and the willow bench — lowest ground
Pooled on top of Granite Knob
options.hint: The knob is the high point. Water doesn't sit there.

options.label: Everywhere equally, because it rained
options.hint: The ridges shed. Look downhill of what you can see from here.

mirror-pond.prompt: The pond is high. Is this where last night's water stopped?

options.label: A pause — water still has a way out
This is the end of the path
options.hint: Look for an outlet, then follow it.

options.label: The rain soaked in here and vanished
options.hint: There's an outlet on the far side.

systems.title: The hollow is a system
systems.lead: Last night wasn't four separate stories. Tap the places that actually took part.
systems.walk: You can close this sketch and inspect the land. The question stays the same.

roles.label: Source
roles.prompt: Tap where last night started — the weather you actually recorded.
roles.miss: Last night started as rain on the gauge, not as a story about trees.

roles.label: Slope
roles.prompt: Tap the loose ground that failed and fed the tributary.
roles.miss: The scar sits on Westface, above Fox Run — not under the pond.

roles.label: Runoff
roles.prompt: Tap the path that carried the brown pulse into Pine Creek.
roles.miss: The station reach stayed relatively clear. The pulse rode Fox Run.

roles.label: Storage
roles.prompt: Tap what held water without starting the mud.
roles.miss: A store holds water. The marsh is tea-colored most days — it didn't fire the pulse.

roles.label: Affected
roles.prompt: Tap what took a hit but did not start the flood.
roles.miss: The willows took a hit. They did not start the mud.

predict.prompt: If Fox Run carried the pulse, tap the reach that should still look clearer.

hints.fox-run: That's where the pulse joined. Look for the stretch that stayed relatively clear.
hints.marsh: The marsh is usually tea-colored. That is storage, not this morning's pulse.
hints.westface: The scar is upstream of the pulse. The clearer water is below the station.
hints.pond: The pond is a pause. The station reach is the comparison.
hints.willows: The roots are hanging in air. They were in the way, not the clearer water.
hints.rain-gauge: The gauge recorded rain. It doesn't tell you which reach stayed clear.
hints.knob: The knob is the high point. Last night's comparison is in the creek.

hints.slope: That's last night's weather, not the scar.
hints.runoff: Rain fell. The pulse still needed a path.
hints.storage: The gauge doesn't hold creek water.
hints.affected: The gauge recorded rain. It didn't take a hit like the willows.

hints.source: The scar is rock and soil, not the rain tally.
hints.runoff: The scar fed Fox Run. The path is the tributary itself.
hints.storage: Loose soil failed here. It didn't store the pulse.
hints.affected: The slope failed. The willows were downstream of that.

hints.source: Fox Run carried water. It didn't make the rain.
hints.slope: The tributary is the path, not the failed slope.
hints.affected: Fox Run is the conveyor. The willows took the hit later.

hints.source: The marsh didn't call the storm.
hints.slope: The scar is on Westface, not in the cattails.
hints.runoff: The pulse joined above the pond, at Fox Run.
hints.affected: Storage isn't the same as the hanging roots.

hints.source: The willows did not call the storm.
hints.slope: The trees didn't fail the hillside.
hints.runoff: The roots are hanging in air. They were in the way, not the engine.
hints.storage: The bank took a hit. The marsh is the store.

hints.source: The pond didn't make the rain.
hints.slope: The pond floor didn't crack. The scar is on Westface.
hints.runoff: The pulse shows up where Fox Run joins, above the pond.
hints.storage: The pond is a pause. The marsh is the store that stayed wet.
hints.affected: The hanging roots are on the willow bank.

hints.source: The station reach stayed relatively clear. Rain started at the gauge.
hints.runoff: This stretch stayed clearer. The pulse rode Fox Run.
hints.affected: The willows are downstream on the cut bank.

hints.source: The knob is the high point. Last night's tally is on the gauge.
hints.slope: The failed soil is Westface, not the summit.
hints.runoff: Water sheds off the knob. The pulse path is Fox Run.
hints.storage: Water doesn't pool on the knob.
hints.affected: The hanging roots are on the willow bank.

conflict.title: When the story breaks
conflict.lead: The crate still says leave the meter in the marsh. The marsh is tea-colored most days. The station reach stayed clear.
conflict.prompt: Does last night's story still hold, or does it need to narrow?

options.label: It rained, so every brown place is the pulse.
options.hint: The stretch by the station stayed clear. Rain fell on more than one place.

options.label: Add the marsh as a second cause and keep the rest.
options.hint: The pulse of mud is above the pond, where the tributary joins. Adding every brown place does not make a better model.

options.label: The pulse is rain on a loose slope into Fox Run. The marsh is its usual color.
Replace the whole story with pond overflow.
options.hint: The brown water shows up where Fox Run joins, above the pond.
